plan: Instrument a maintainer test build to correlate foreground HWND/generation, eligibility checks and ShellWindows registration, comparing new Explorer windows, existing windows and Ctrl+Space without changing user settings between observations.

Choose bounded asynchronous retry or a shell-registration-triggered recomputation only for the demonstrated transient case. Bind results to the current foreground generation and cancel pending work on foreground change, mode disable or module destruction.

Preserve non-Explorer/editing behavior and COM/thread ownership. Do not blanket-extend the timer or add blocking shell enumeration to an input-hook callback; add regression coverage for transient false results and obsolete callbacks.
verification: With Space-only enabled, repeatedly open a new Explorer window and select a file without switching focus; activation recovers after shell registration without toggling settings.
Use controlled registration delay beyond40ms and rapid foreground changes; obsolete checks must not mark a different window eligible or produce unbounded background work.
Compare Ctrl+Space, existing Explorer windows, desktop, text-edit controls and unrelated applications; disable/unload Peek with a pending callback and verify safe cancellation.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A one-shot40ms eligibility check may precede the newly foreground Explorer window registration. Space-only activation then consumes a cached false result rather than reevaluating after registration; this is a supported mechanism, not independently reproduced timing.

confidence.rationale: Exact-release/current control flow matches the contributor timing and multiple historical workarounds. Runtime reproduction and safe asynchronous invalidation/lifecycle design remain outstanding.

proposed_fixes.title: Recover Peek eligibility after delayed Explorer registration

reproduce.expected: Eligible Explorer selection activates Peek reliably after registration without manual shortcut reset; ordinary space typing elsewhere and callback cleanup remain unchanged.
steps: Open a new Explorer window, select a file and try Space without changing settings or moving focus away.
If rejected, leave the same window foreground long enough for registration and retry; compare switching focus away/back and Ctrl+Space as separate controls.
Correlate the cached negative result with registration timing, then exercise delayed registration, rapid foreground changes and module disable against any candidate cache-recovery design.
prerequisites: Windows Explorer and Peek with Enable Space to activate enabled.
Maintainer-instrumented build for correlation of foreground generation, eligibility result and shell registration; no reporter profiling is requested.
reproduce.version: Reported0.95.0 through0.100.2; relevant source checked at0.102.3001 and current main

inferences: A foreground check before shell registration can explain persistent negative eligibility for one window; original settings-reset symptoms may include an additional initialization path.
issue_context.analysis: The newly supplied timing explains the focus-away-and-back workaround more specifically than a generic shortcut-reset diagnosis. A negative result can outlive the transient registration gap because Space-only activation consults the cache until another recomputation. Maintainer reproduction should distinguish delayed shell registration from first-run setting initialization and retain Ctrl+Space as a control. Medium impact if unfixed: affected new Explorer windows can reject Space activation until focus or settings change, making the default workflow unreliable; no data-loss or crash claim is established.
issue_context.summary: Investigate a stale-negative foreground eligibility cache in Space-only Peek activation; the latest contributor supplies a measured Explorer-registration race.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report, discussion and timeline, including the latest contributor measurement and earlier focus-change controls.
Inspected immutable v0.102.3001 and current-main src/modules/peek/peek/dllmain.cpp: debounce, cache store, ShellWindows enumeration and the two on_hotkey branches.
No independent timing experiment, UI reproduction, product modification or shipped-fix claim is made. This is a lightweight maintainer investigation proposal, not an approved full design.
known_information: Original0.95.0 report says changing the shortcut and restoring Space temporarily enables activation. Later reports describe newly opened Explorer windows recovering after focus leaves and returns, while Ctrl+Space works.

The latest contributor reports reproducing on several machines with0.100.2 and measures one Explorer HWND appearing in IShellWindows271ms after becoming foreground. That timing and their log counts are contributor observations, not independently executed measurements.
Immutable v0.102.3001 and current-main Peek source use a40ms one-shot foreground debounce and cache the result of is_peek_or_explorer_or_desktop_window_focused in g_foregroundEligible.
In on_hotkey, Space-only mode with an active foreground hook reads the cached boolean; the other branch checks eligibility live. IShellWindows enumeration compares registered HWNDs.

The source mechanism supports a stale-negative race when shell registration follows the one-shot check. It does not prove that every initial-setting symptom has that cause or that one fixed delay is sufficient.
